context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud platform. It processes online claims and adjuster workflows while keeping the legacy COBOL/DB2 system as the system of record.]

## Key Elements
- [Customer & Broker Portal (Web/Mobile)]
- [Modern Claims Platform: API Management, Claims Web App, Claim Routing Service, Claims Processing Service]
- [Data Storage: Azure SQL Database]
- [Integration Gateway: Azure Service Bus, On-Premises Integration Service]
- [External Systems: Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2, IBM MQ), Active Directory / Entra ID Connect]

## Relationships
- [Customer & Broker Portal -> Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS/REST]
- [Adjusters -> Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS/WebSockets]
- [Modern Claims Platform -> Active Directory: HTTPS (OIDC/SAML)]
- [Claim Routing Service -> Azure SQL Database: TDS via Entity Framework Core]
- [Modern Claims Platform -> Azure Service Bus -> On-Premises Integration Service: AMQP]
- [On-Premises Integration Service -> Legacy Mainframe: IBM MQ protocol]

## Technology Stack
- [Azure App Service & Azure Container Apps: Simplifies cloud operations for a team with limited cloud experience]
- [Azure SQL Database: Provides cloud data persistence with rollback capability for migrated claim types]
- [Azure Service Bus & IBM MQ: Enables asynchronous, decoupled hybrid messaging respecting batch windows]
- [Azure API Management & Key Vault: Secures ingress and manages secrets via Managed Identity]

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture safely isolates fragile mainframe touchpoints while leveraging managed cloud services to reduce operational complexity. Asynchronous messaging and dynamic routing guarantee zero data loss and enable rapid fallback to the legacy system within one day.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
This system gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform with a modern, hybrid cloud architecture. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining seamless integration with the legacy system during a multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal (React/TypeScript SPA)
* Web Frontend (React/TypeScript SPA)
* API Gateway / BFF (Node.js/Express)
* Claims Core Service (.NET 8 / C#)
* Integration & Sync Worker (Python/C# Azure Function)
* Claims Database (Azure SQL Database Managed Instance)
* Integration Event Broker (Azure Service Bus)
* Distributed Cache / State Store (Azure Cache for Redis)
* Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration)
* Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 on-premises)

## Relationships
* Customer Portal & Web Frontend -> API Gateway / BFF via HTTPS/REST and WSS (JSON)
* API Gateway / BFF -> Claims Core Service via gRPC / HTTP/2
* Claims Core Service -> Claims Database via TDS over TLS (TCP 1433)
* Claims Core Service -> Integration Event Broker via AMQP over TLS (TCP 5671)
* Integration & Sync Worker -> Legacy Mainframe via secure SFTP/MQ
* API Gateway / BFF and SPAs -> Azure AD / Entra ID via OpenID Connect (OIDC) over HTTPS
* Claims Core Service -> Configuration & Feature Store via HTTPS/REST

## Technology Stack
* Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts frontend SPAs for regional users
* Azure Container Apps: Runs containerized microservices and BFF to simplify cloud operations
* .NET 8 / C# and Node.js: Core backend and API runtime technologies
* Azure SQL Database: Provides relational persistence and ACID consistency for migrated claims
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronously decouples services to prevent data loss and protect legacy batch limits
* Azure Cache for Redis: Handles distributed session caching and idempotency keys
* Azure App Configuration: Enables dynamic feature flagging for rapid claim-type switch-backs

## Rationale
Fully managed Azure PaaS services compensate for the team's limited cloud experience while lowering operational overhead. Asynchronous messaging and dynamic configuration routing successfully isolate expensive mainframe dependencies and satisfy strict migration, performance, and consistency constraints.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring uninterrupted legacy processing and zero claim loss. It enables online submissions and modern adjuster workflows via Azure-hosted containers integrated securely with Active Directory.

## Key Elements
- Customer Portal (React / TypeScript SPA)
- API Gateway / BFF (Node.js / Express)
- Claims Core Service (.NET 8 / C#)
- Integration & Sync Worker (Python / C# Azure Function)
- Claims Database (Azure SQL Database Managed Instance)
- Integration Event Broker (Azure Service Bus)
- Distributed Cache (Azure Cache for Redis)
- Configuration Store (Azure App Configuration)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Azure AD / Entra ID

## Relationships
- Customer & Broker -> Customer Portal: Submits and tracks claims [HTTPS]
- Customer Portal -> API Gateway / BFF: Sends API requests and WebSocket messages [HTTPS/REST, WSS]
- API Gateway / BFF -> Claims Core Service: Dispatches commands and queries [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Claims Core Service -> Claims Database: Persists and retrieves claim data [ADO.NET / Entity Framework Core]
- Claims Core Service -> Integration Event Broker: Publishes domain events [AMQP over TLS]
- Integration & Sync Worker -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes data [Batch / Secure File Transfer / Proprietary Protocols]
- Customer Portal & API Gateway -> Azure AD / Entra ID: Authenticates and validates users [OIDC / OAuth2 / JWKS over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React with TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, and Zustand for lightweight state management and caching
- Backend Gateway: Node.js with Express, TypeScript, and `ws` for WebSocket handling
- Core Services: .NET 8 / C# for robust, high-performance domain logic
- Database & Cache: Azure SQL Database Managed Instance and Azure Cache for Redis for transactional consistency and fast retrieval
- Messaging: Azure Service Bus for reliable asynchronous event distribution
- Cloud & Identity: Hybrid deployment on Azure West Europe and on-premises mainframe, secured via Azure AD / Entra ID

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes while safely migrating claim types incrementally over three years. It combines modern cloud scalability and performance with strict consistency guarantees to prevent duplicate or lost claims.

Web Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform with a modern hybrid cloud architecture. It ensures zero data loss, high performance, and rapid fallback capabilities during the three-year migration.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customers, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters
- **External Systems**: Legacy Mainframe, Azure AD / Entra ID Connect
- **Web Frontend**: React / TypeScript Single Page Application (SPA)
- **API Gateway / BFF**: Node.js / Express backend-for-frontend
- **Claims Core Service**: .NET 8 / C# core domain service
- **Integration & Sync Worker**: Python / C# Azure Functions
- **Data & Messaging**: Azure SQL Database, Azure Service Bus, Azure Cache for Redis, Azure App Configuration

## Relationships
- *Customer Portal / Web Frontend* -> *Azure AD / Entra ID*: Authenticates users [OpenID Connect (OIDC) over HTTPS]
- *Web Frontend* -> *API Gateway / BFF*: Sends API requests and WebSocket messages [HTTPS/REST, WSS (JSON)]
- *API Gateway / BFF* -> *Claims Core Service*: Forwards internal commands and queries [gRPC / HTTPS]
- *Integration & Sync Worker* -> *Legacy Mainframe*: Synchronizes claims data [Batch / Secure File Transfer]
- *Claims Core Service* -> *Azure Service Bus*: Publishes and consumes domain events [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: React and TypeScript to minimize custom framework lock-in given limited team cloud experience
- **Backend / Services**: Node.js / Express for the BFF layer; .NET 8 / C# for robust core domain processing
- **Cloud Provider**: Azure (westeurope region) combined with on-premise mainframe integration for a secure hybrid setup
- **Data & State**: Azure SQL Database Managed Instance for relational persistence; Azure Cache for Redis for distributed caching; Azure Service Bus for asynchronous messaging

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while introducing a modern cloud platform via strangulation. It directly satisfies stringent performance (R-05) and fallback (R-06) constraints without requiring extensive prior cloud experience from the engineering team.

API Gateway / BFF.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid modernization platform for a regional insurer that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system. Its core purpose is to provide modern online claim submission and adjuster portals while keeping the legacy mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer & Broker, Claims Adjusters
- **Edge Routing**: Azure API Management (APIM)
- **Frontends**: Customer Portal (React / TypeScript SPA), Web Frontend (React / TypeScript SPA)
- **BFF / Gateway Components**: Customer BFF (Node.js / Express), Adjuster BFF (Node.js / Express with WebSocket Gateway Module)
- **Backend Services**: Claims Core Service (.NET 8 / C#), Integration & Sync Worker (Python / C# Azure Function)
- **Data & Caching**: Azure SQL Database Managed Instance, Azure Cache for Redis
- **Messaging**: Azure Service Bus (Integration Event Broker)
- **External Systems**: Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe, Azure Active Directory / Entra ID

## Relationships
- Customer Portal & Web Frontend -> Azure API Management [HTTPS, WSS]
- Azure API Management -> Customer BFF & Adjuster BFF [HTTP/2, internal vNet]
- Adjuster BFF -> Azure Cache for Redis [TCP/RESP]
- Azure Service Bus -> Adjuster BFF (WebSocket Gateway) [AMQP / Azure SDK]
- Customer BFF & Adjuster BFF -> Claims Core Service [gRPC]
- Azure API Management -> Azure Active Directory [OpenID Connect (OIDC) over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Edge Security**: Azure APIM for managed rate-limiting, SSL termination, and OIDC token validation to reduce operational overhead.
- **Frontend Runtimes**: Node.js with Express for lightweight, decoupled BFFs tailored to customer and adjuster workflows.
- **Caching & Real-Time**: Azure Cache for Redis to mitigate 5-second mainframe latencies, and Socket.io/ws for real-time WebSocket push updates.
- **Backend & Integration**: .NET 8 for core claims services, Python/C# Azure Functions for sync workers, and Azure Service Bus for event-driven messaging.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive-to-change mainframe while modernizing the user experience via Azure-hosted cloud services. It successfully meets strict performance and consistency constraints despite the team's low initial cloud experience.

Claims Core Service.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe by gradually migrating claims processing to a hybrid Azure cloud platform. The architecture ensures business continuity, maintaining the legacy system as the system of record during the transition.

## Key Elements
- Feature Routing Dispatcher (.NET class library)
- Claim Command Processor (.NET class library using MediatR)
- Claim Query Handler (.NET class library)
- Domain Model / Aggregate Roots (.NET class library)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (.NET class library)
- Mainframe Adapter Component (.NET class library)
- Idempotency Validator (StackExchange.Redis)
- Integration Event Publisher (Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus)

## Relationships
- Feature Routing Dispatcher -> Claim Command Processor: Delegates modern claim workflows [Internal C# Method Call]
- Feature Routing Dispatcher -> Mainframe Adapter Component: Delegates legacy fallback workflows [Internal C# Method Call]
- Claim Command Processor -> Idempotency Validator: Checks duplicate processing [Redis Protocol over TLS]
- Claim Command Processor -> Domain Model / Aggregate Roots: Executes business rules [Internal C# Method Call]
- Domain Model -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Translates domain models to legacy structures [Internal C# Method Call]
- Domain Model -> Integration Event Publisher: Emits state change events [AMQP over TLS (TCP 5671)]
- Claim Query Handler -> Claims Database: Reads optimized claim data [TDS over TLS (TCP 1433)]

## Technology Stack
- .NET 8 / C#: Chosen for core business logic implementation, aligning with team capabilities
- MediatR: Implements CQRS pattern to separate command and query workloads
- StackExchange.Redis: Manages distributed caching for idempotency and session state
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous, reliable integration event messaging
- Azure App Configuration: Stores dynamic feature flags for real-time fallback routing

## Rationale
The component architecture cleanly isolates legacy integration complexities to support a one-day rollback constraint. Additionally, it optimizes query performance to meet sub-second response targets despite underlying hybrid latency limitations.

## Rationale

Claims Database.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a modern cloud-based claims platform designed to gradually replace a legacy mainframe claims system for a regional insurer. It ensures seamless hybrid operations, strict data consistency, and rapid rollback capabilities during a multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
* **Claim Tables**: Core relational Azure SQL storage enforcing strict ACID guarantees for migrated claim types.
* **Sync Staging Tables**: Azure SQL staging area for asynchronous replication payloads managed by the integration worker.
* **Audit & Temporal History**: Azure SQL System-Versioned Temporal Tables tracking historical row versions for compliance and rollback.
* **Change Tracking Mechanism**: Azure SQL Change Tracking feature capturing row-level changes asynchronously without table locks.
* **Reconciliation & Rollback Views**: Azure SQL Views encapsulating complex JOINs to expose unified payload views for verification and rollback.

## Relationships
* **Claims Core Service** -> **Claim Tables & Audit History**: Executes domain queries via TDS over TLS (TCP 1433).
* **Integration & Sync Worker** -> **Sync Staging Tables**: Stages reconciliation data via TDS over TLS (TCP 1433).
* **Integration & Sync Worker** -> **Change Tracking Mechanism**: Polls delta changes via TDS over TLS (TCP 1433).
* **Integration & Sync Worker** -> **Reconciliation & Rollback Views**: Reads unified snapshots via TDS over TLS (TCP 1433).

## Technology Stack
* **Azure SQL Database Managed Instance**: Provides relational persistence and ACID consistency.
* **T-SQL**: Used for defining tables, views, and system tracking features.
* **TDS over TLS (TCP 1433)**: Secure protocol for all database connectivity.

## Rationale
This component architecture fits requirements by utilizing native database capabilities for change tracking and temporal history, ensuring zero data loss and strict consistency during hybrid synchronization. Furthermore, it supports the strict nightly batch window and enables rapid one-day rollbacks of migrated claim types to the legacy mainframe.

## Overview
The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance mainframe claims platform by gradually migrating claim types to a new cloud-based architecture. It uses a hybrid cloud model to ensure continuous operations and zero data loss during the 3-year migration window.

## Key Elements

- Azure SQL Database Managed Instance: Relational data store for migrated claims.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Distributed caching and state management for performance.
- Python / C#: Lightweight workers for legacy mainframe synchronization and batch processing.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while delivering a modern sub-second user experience. It guarantees zero data loss (R-04) and rapid one-day fallback (R-06) via event-driven decoupling and strict state synchronization.

  - Eviction & Expiration Policy Engine (`volatile-lru`)
- Claims Core Service -> Distributed Cache / State Store: Manages session cache and idempotency [Redis RESP / TCP over TLS]
- Integration & Sync Worker -> Idempotency State Manager: Prevents event replay [Redis RESP / TCP over TLS]
- Claims Core Service -> Migration Routing & Fallback Cache: Evaluates migration status [Redis RESP / TCP over TLS]
- Integration & Sync Worker -> Distributed Lock Manager: Acquires synchronization locks [Redis RESP / TCP over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure (West Europe) & On-Premise Hybrid: Matches infrastructure constraints and data residency needs.
- React & TypeScript: Modern responsive SPA frameworks for customer portal and adjuster web apps.
- Node.js & Express: Lightweight API Gateway / BFF for frontend routing.
- .NET 8 / C#: Robust enterprise runtime for the core claims processing logic.
- Azure SQL Database Managed Instance: Fully managed relational database ensuring ACID consistency for migrated claims.
- Azure Service Bus: Reliable message broker for asynchronous event-driven integration.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Low-latency distributed cache satisfying sub-2-second adjuster screen performance goals (R-05).
- Azure App Configuration: Centralized management of application settings and feature flags.
- Python / C# Azure Functions: Flexible serverless workers for background synchronization and integration tasks.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture balances low-risk incremental migration with strict consistency requirements, ensuring no claims are lost or duplicated while isolating expensive mainframe interactions. Redis caching and asynchronous synchronization bridge legacy performance gaps, enabling sub-2-second UI responses and 1-day fallback capabilities despite limited team cloud experience.

Configuration & Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims platform through a hybrid cloud architecture, enabling gradual claim type migration while maintaining business continuity. It provides online claim submission and adjuster web portals backed by Azure cloud services and an on-premise mainframe system of record.]

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal and Web Frontend (React / TypeScript SPA)
* API Gateway / BFF (Node.js / Express)
* Claims Core Service (.NET 8 / C#)
* Integration & Sync Worker (Python / C# Azure Function)
* Claims Database (Azure SQL Database Managed Instance)
* Integration Event Broker (Azure Service Bus)
* Distributed Cache / State Store (Azure Cache for Redis)
* Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration)
* External Systems: Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2) and Active Directory / Entra ID

## Relationships
* Customer Portal / Web Frontend -> API Gateway / BFF: Routes user requests [HTTPS/REST]
* API Gateway / BFF -> Claims Core Service: Forwards processed claims and UI requests [gRPC / HTTPS]
* Claims Core Service -> Claims Database: Persists modern claim records [T-SQL / TDS]
* Claims Core Service -> Integration Event Broker: Publishes and consumes domain events [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
* Integration & Sync Worker -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes data between cloud and legacy systems [Batch / MQ]
* Claims Core Service / BFF -> Configuration & Feature Store: Evaluates feature flags and dynamic routing rules [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
* Frontend: React with TypeScript for modern responsive user interfaces
* Backend Services: Node.js / Express for BFF and .NET 8 / C# for core domain processing
* Database: Azure SQL Database Managed Instance for relational claim data storage
* Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus for asynchronous messaging and Azure Event Grid for event routing
* Configuration: Azure App Configuration with Key Vault references for dynamic feature toggles and secure secrets

## Rationale
* The hybrid cloud approach isolates legacy mainframe constraints while incrementally migrating business capabilities to Azure. 
* Azure App Configuration and event-driven caching ensure sub-second feature toggles required for rapid rollback constraints.
